summary: Nex Core installs /var/lib/libvirt/images by default; Controller auto-registers it as storage named ISO on the first managed host report (request_id auto-storage:<host>), matching auto-network behavior. API impact: existing contract — reuses storage-register; documents auto-storage.

guide.reason: VM creation prerequisites and steps now use the automatic ISO storage registration instead of requiring manual Register local storage first.

api.reason: No new endpoint or schema field. Controller queues the existing storage-register command for /var/lib/libvirt/images named ISO, same as auto-network for bridges. Documented in API.md and OpenAPI StorageRegistration semantics.

state.reason: The default ISO storage is an ordinary pool-scoped storage registration auto-issued by the Controller and persisted on the pool master.
state.record: storage-register entry with request_id auto-storage:<host> in the managed journal on the pool master (internal/vmhost, /var/lib/nex/core-local/vmhost/<operation-id>.json): the accepted command and its result are the durable record; the host reports them as Inventory.managed and a fresh Controller re-adopts them with the same IDs and names through adoptManaged. The Controller managed_resources rows are a mirror.

verification.method: go test ./internal/controller -run 'TestManaged|TestDefault|TestHostReported|TestVLAN'; python3 scripts/generate_api.py (and --check). Live host enrollment + Storage UI showing ISO succeeded remains a lab walkthrough.
